new.managementAccessHint: Opens api-ssl (8729, management range only, a certificate made on the router) on each router in service, over SSH, one job per router. The waves are the server's ladder (canary first, behind the health gate); no dead-man is armed, a pre-change backup is taken before each first write. Where a router lacks ObliWAN's own "obliwan" account, the job creates it and switches ObliWAN to it once a login with it is proven. Where the "obliwan" group ObliWAN made lacks only the "sensitive" policy, the job adds it — the one existing account or group it changes — through the historical "admin" account from the vault (admin_password) on a router already reached as "obliwan"; without that credential, a router with nothing else to write succeeds and says the group is not aligned; one where api-ssl must still be written fails at its pre-change backup (nothing is written) until the group is aligned.

new.noPublishedRevision: This template has no published revision: publish one on the Templates page first.
new.serverWaves: The server composes the waves: 1 router (the canary), then up to 5 %, 25 %, then the rest — routers without remote recovery last.
new.gatePolicyManualRestore: Between two waves the health gate decides. A rollout that fails it stops for a human: nothing is undone automatically. A template push also has its revision quarantined, and every router that took the change is listed « To undo »: a rollout of the previous revision to those routers undoes it. An inconclusive gate pauses the rollout.
new.compositionChanged: The server composed a different rollout than the one shown (a router was refused or reordered since the impact screen). The draft was aborted and nothing was queued: recompute the impact radius.
new.legacyComplianceHint: Brings each router in service up to the corrected customer templates, over SSH with its existing account (no user is created), one job per router: mac-server and mac-winbox on every interface, RoMON on, the DNS-Amp rules where missing, the store LAN added to restricted ssh and winbox lists. random-source-port is read and reported, never written: no line restarts the tunnels. The waves are the server’s ladder (canary first, behind the health gate); a pre-change backup is taken before each first write.
new.wanLinkHint: Switches the fixed line (WAN1) of each store to the chosen mode, one job per router, its parameters read from each site's variables (PPPoE login and the password in the site's vault, fixed address and gateway): a site missing one is refused by name. Each job checks the 4G first, cuts the fixed line on purpose and starts ONE script on the router, which puts the old link back by itself if the new one carries no traffic. The waves are the server's ladder (canary first, behind the health gate); a pre-change backup is taken before each switch.
new.wanLinkCutConfirmHint: Each store's fixed line is CUT while its router switches: the store rides its 4G, and its down and 4G alerts are held for the duration of its job. A router whose new link carries no traffic puts the old one back by itself. This confirmation is recorded with your name.

explainer.for: The condition must hold without interruption for this long before anybody is notified. Without it, a single 30-second spike wakes the on-call engineer. This is the setting that turns a transient into a non-event.
explainer.hysteresis: Once the alert is firing, the value must come back this far past the threshold before it clears. Without it, a value parked on the boundary fires, clears, fires and clears again on every polling cycle, forever.
explainer.mandatory: Both fields are mandatory and carry no default: the database refuses a threshold that omits them, on purpose. A value you did not choose is a value nobody can explain during an incident.
explainer.title: Dwell time and hysteresis — the two settings that stop alert storms

hints.forSeconds: How long the condition must hold before the alert fires. Below the polling interval it has no effect; two polling cycles is a sensible starting point.
hints.hysteresis: Expressed as a percentage of the threshold value. 10 % on a threshold of 80 % means the alert clears below 72 %.
hints.hysteresisZero: With no hysteresis, a value sitting exactly on the threshold will fire and clear on every polling cycle.

lanReprise.title: Record the LAN of existing sites

Each site must already be allocated (adopted from the CHR or allocated). Its LAN is recorded on its allocation, so lan_subnet and the values derived from it (lan_router_ip…) resolve for it, and no later allocation hands out an address inside it. Nothing is written to any router.

concentratorLink.intro: ObliWAN reaches the sites' tunnel addresses (100.64.0.0/10) through a WireGuard link to this concentrator, which masquerades that traffic: nothing changes on the sites.
concentratorLink.hostBoundTo: The ObliWAN host already follows {{name}}: it carries one WireGuard link for all of 100.64.0.0/10, so this concentrator cannot be connected as well. ObliWAN has no operation that unbinds a link.

concentratorLink.confirmBody: This job only ADDS items on the concentrator: a WireGuard interface, an address, a peer, accept rules and one masquerade rule limited to ObliWAN's transit address. It never modifies or removes anything, and arms no dead-man: nothing it adds can cut the path ObliWAN uses to manage the concentrator (its public address). Before its first write it must take a backup of the concentrator; if that backup cannot be taken, the job stops at that step and writes nothing. The step says why.
concentratorLink.switchExplain: Separate step, once the link is proven: ObliWAN then manages this concentrator through {{address}} instead of its public address, which is kept as the fallback.

concentratorLink.revert: Go back to the public address
concentratorLink.operatorTitle: To do by hand on the concentrator (ObliWAN never does it)
concentratorLink.operatorWarn: This restricts the API service to ObliWAN through the tunnel. Do not touch the winbox and ssh services: keep your own access, and test from a second session before closing yours. If you use the API yourself from elsewhere, add your address to the list. It also closes the public fallback above until you widen it again.

managementAccess.title: Management access (API-SSL)
managementAccess.intro: ObliWAN manages this router through its RouterOS API over TLS: api-ssl on 8729, open to the management range only, serving a certificate generated on the router, whose fingerprint ObliWAN pins on first contact. The job goes through SSH with the existing account; where the router lacks ObliWAN's own account "obliwan", it creates it (restricted to the management range) and switches ObliWAN's API and SSH channels to it once a login with it is proven. No other user is touched.

legacyCompliance.title: Compliance (template fixes)
legacyCompliance.intro: The corrections made to the customer templates, applied to this router in service by a change job over SSH with its existing account — no user is created. MAC-telnet, MAC-Winbox and RoMON are only ever opened, an address is only ever added to the ssh and winbox lists (the store LAN, read on the router), and the two DNS-Amp rules (DNS from the WAN list rejected) are added where missing. random-source-port on the L2TP clients is read and shown, never written: the right value depends on the site’s operator and box, and the value of a router that works is never changed. siteRename.title: Site rename
siteRename.intro: Renames this router's PPP login on the shared concentrator, the user of its management tunnel (l2tp-mgmt), its identity and, if asked, the site code — together, by one guarded job.
